question: What does public accountability primarily require a nurse manager to do?

options.A: Increase the monthly budget of the facility
options.B: Answer for resource usage and clinical outcomes
options.C: Handle disciplinary cases among junior doctors
options.D: Purchase private equipment for the hospital ward

explanation: Public accountability centers on stewardship and answering to stakeholders for operational decisions, resource allocation, and patient care outcomes. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h1)

question: A nurse leader fails to manage ward supplies well, leading to medicine shortages. Which concept has this leader violated?
explanation: Wasting or mismanaging public resources entrusted to a nurse manager violates the core principles of public accountability. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h1)

question: Which body is empowered by an Act to regulate nursing practice and training in Nigeria?

options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NMCN derives its legal mandate from an Act of Parliament to regulate all tiers of nursing education and clinical practice in Nigeria. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h2)

question: Why must a public health nurse leader understand civil service rules and health acts?

options.A: To bypass financial auditing processes completely
options.B: To prescribe medications independently to patients
options.C: To replace the hospital chief medical director
options.D: To ensure administrative decisions stay within legal boundaries

explanation: Compliance with civil service rules and health acts protects the administrator and the health institution from legal liabilities and malpractice. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of checks and balances in a public hospital?

options.A: Eliminating the need for external government oversight
options.B: Slowing down emergency care delivery in the wards
options.C: Preventing any single individual from holding absolute power
options.D: Ensuring doctors earn higher salaries than nurses

explanation: Distributing power and duties among different offices prevents abuse, corruption, and unilateral decision-making. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h3)

question: A nurse unit manager wants to purchase new oxygen cylinders. Following checks and balances, who should verify the delivery before payment?

options.A: The same nurse manager who ordered them
options.B: The external police force in the state
options.C: An independent store officer or internal audit unit
options.D: Patients admitted to the accident and emergency ward

explanation: Separating the ordering function from the verification and payment functions ensures proper internal control and transparency. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h3)

question: Funds generated directly by a public health facility through services are referred to as what?
explanation: Internally generated revenue (IGR) represents fees and collections made directly by the hospital from patient services and other commercial ventures. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h4)

question: Which activity is a direct violation of financial integrity in nursing administration?

options.A: Consulting staff before drafting the annual ward budget
options.B: Padding budget estimates to siphon public funds
options.C: Requesting more syringes for an overcrowded emergency ward
options.D: Reporting damaged equipment to the maintenance unit

explanation: Budget padding to misappropriate public funds directly breaches financial integrity and anti-corruption regulations. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h4)

question: Who conducts external financial audits for public institutions in Nigeria?

options.B: The head pharmacist of the facility

explanation: External audits are legally mandated to be carried out by independent supreme audit institutions like the Auditor-General's office. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h5)

question: Why are routine internal audits important in a public health facility?

options.A: To increase the prices of drugs at the hospital pharmacy
options.B: To replace the need for professional nursing supervision
options.C: To punish nurses who refuse to work night shifts
options.D: To catch financial errors and discrepancies early before external audits

explanation: Internal audits act as an early warning system to correct financial mistakes and prevent fraud before statutory external auditors review the books. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h5)

question: What is a primary ethical duty of a nurse leader facing institutional wrongdoing?

options.A: Blaming junior nursing students for the mistake
options.B: Reporting the wrongdoing and protecting whistleblowers
options.C: Ignoring the incident to maintain peace among staff

explanation: Ethical nursing leadership demands professional courage to expose corruption and safeguard those who report malpractice. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h6)

question: A nurse manager assigns choice shifts only to personal friends while ignoring equitable rostering. This violates which professional value?
explanation: Showing bias in duty rostering violates the ethical standard of fairness and destroys team morale in the workplace. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h6)

question: A patient is asked to pay a bribe before receiving emergency treatment in a public clinic. What mechanism should address this grievance?

options.A: Ignoring the complaint to protect the hospital's image
options.B: A functional hospital complaint desk and anti-corruption unit
options.C: Public protests outside the ministry of works
options.D: Immediate dismissal of all nursing staff on duty

explanation: Institutions require structured grievance redress channels like complaint desks and anti-corruption units to investigate and resolve extortion claims. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common manifestation of maladministration in public hospitals?

options.A: Extortion of informal fees from vulnerable patients
options.B: Chronic staff absenteeism from assigned clinical wards
options.C: Prompt and equitable delivery of patient care to all
options.D: Diversion of government-supplied drugs to private chemist shops

explanation: Prompt and equitable care represents good governance and high-quality administration, not maladministration. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h7)
